pages.name: Quick Start
pages.content:
Setting Up and Using Minefields

Minefields are automated with a Minefield Region Behavior on a Scene. The Region defines who can trigger it and stores its detection, density, condition, direct-hit, and blast settings.

GM Quick Start

  1. Open the Scene and switch to the Region controls.
  2. Draw a Region over the hazardous area.
  3. Open the Region configuration, add a Behavior, and choose Minefield.
  4. Configure the minefield and save the Region.
  5. Move a compatible token into or within the Region.
  6. In the movement dialog, choose the movement method, scout, affected hexes crossed, and number of entrants.
  7. Review the result in chat. If a mine detonates, use the GM buttons to apply direct damage and resolve the blast against selected tokens.

The movement resolver is handled by the primary active GM. Players may move their own tokens, but a GM must be connected for the automation to resolve the crossing.

Important

A successful detection marks the Behavior as Discovered and ends that crossing before a trigger check. Discovery does not automatically reveal the Region's shape to players; the GM can reveal or mark the danger on the Scene as appropriate.

pages.name: Creating the Region
pages.content:
Creating the Region

  1. Activate the Scene that will contain the minefield.
  2. Select the Region tool from the Scene controls.
  3. Draw a polygon, rectangle, ellipse, or freehand Region covering the hazardous area.
  4. Open the new Region's configuration.
  5. Open its Behaviors section, add a Behavior, and select Minefield.
  6. Configure the Behavior, then save both the Behavior and Region.

The Minefield Behavior listens for a token entering the Region and for movement within it. A movement that crosses several affected hexes can be resolved in one dialog by entering the total number of affected hexes crossed.

Which Tokens Are Affected?

  • Anti-Personnel: Characters and NPCs.
  • Anti-Vehicle: Vehicles.
  • Mixed: Characters, NPCs, and Vehicles.
  • Water: only Vehicles whose domain is Watercraft or Amphibious and whose Size is above the configured safe limit.

Actor types that do not match the Behavior are ignored. A Region may contain multiple Behaviors, but avoid overlapping duplicate Minefield Behaviors unless you deliberately want separate hazards to resolve.

Explosive Items

Explosive Items can represent individual carried or placed mines. They are not linked to a Minefield Region automatically. Copy the desired values into the Region Behavior when building an area hazard.

pages.name: Minefield Configuration
pages.content:
Minefield Configuration

Area and Reliability

  • Environment: choose Land or Water.
  • Density: False makes no trigger checks; Sparse checks one entrant per crossed hex; Normal checks up to two entrants per crossed hex; Dense checks every entrant for every crossed hex.
  • Condition: Fresh mines do not make a dud result; Old mines are duds on a dud-roll result of 1; Overgrown mines are duds on 1–2.
  • Mine Type: Anti-Personnel, Anti-Vehicle, or Mixed controls which land Actors can trigger the field.

Damage Profile

  • Direct Damage: base damage applied to the token that triggered the mine.
  • Critical Rating: the direct hit's critical-injury threshold.
  • Blast Rating: A–D enables a separate blast resolution for nearby selected tokens; a dash disables it.
  • Armor Modifier: applied when the mine tests armor.
  • Airburst: prevents prone targets from reducing the Blast rating.
  • Directional: tells the blast resolver to use a directed area. The GM selects only tokens inside that area and reduces Blast one step for every three hexes when prompted.

Detection

  • Detection Modifier: an additional modifier on the automatic detection roll. Positive values make detection easier and negative values make it harder.
  • Discovered: marks the field as already known, skipping future automatic detection rolls. It does not make the minefield harmless.

Give each Region a descriptive GM-facing name. The name appears in the movement and detection messages and makes overlapping hazards easier to manage.

pages.name: Skills and Mine Actions
pages.content:
Skills and Mine Actions

World Skill Configuration

The GM can open Game Settings → Configure Settings → System Settings → Action Skills and assign the world's Skill Items for:

  • Detect mines
  • Move cautiously through mines
  • Probe for mines
  • Place mines
  • Clear mines
  • Water-mine avoidance

This is important in worlds that use custom Skill names. Every participating Actor needs an embedded copy of the configured Skill.

Character Actions

The following actions are available through Take Action or a relevant Skill roll:

  • Detect mines: a free, reactive detection test.
  • Move cautiously through mines: a Fast Action for a cautious one-hex crossing.
  • Probe for mines: an extended task taking one stretch, with a +2 modifier.
  • Place mines: an extended task taking one stretch.
  • Clear mines: an extended task taking one stretch for one hex. Failure warns that a mine may detonate.

The action controls track actions and make the appropriate Skill rolls. They do not draw, resize, remove, or disable Regions. After a successful Place or Clear action, the GM must create or edit the affected Minefield Region. After a failed Clear action, the GM should resolve the relevant hazard.

The Region movement dialog does not itself spend a Fast or Slow Action. When combat action economy matters, use the appropriate Character action as well as resolving the token's movement through the Region.

pages.name: Movement and Detection
pages.content:
Movement and Detection

When a compatible token enters or moves within the Region, the primary active GM receives Resolve Minefield Movement.

Movement Method

  • Unaware Movement: ordinary movement through an unknown hazard. Trigger checks use a D6.
  • Cautious Movement: use when the group is moving cautiously through the affected area. Trigger checks still use a D6.
  • Probing: grants +2 to detection and changes trigger checks to a D10, reducing the chance of a trigger.

Scout

Select the Character or NPC making the detection check. The menu lists suitable Actors represented by tokens on the current Scene. Choose No detection check when nobody can scout, or when the GM has already resolved detection separately.

If the Behavior is not already Discovered, the system rolls the configured Detect Mines Skill privately to the GM. Overgrown fields impose −2, anti-vehicle mines grant +2, and detecting from a Vehicle imposes −2; the Region's Detection Modifier and the probing bonus are also applied. Detection cannot be pushed.

On a success, the Behavior is marked Discovered, a detection message is posted, and no trigger check is made for that crossing.

Affected Hexes and Entrants

Enter only the number of hexes covered by the Minefield Region, not the token's entire movement. Entrants is the number of people or vehicles exposed together during that movement. Density determines how many entrants are checked in each affected hex.

Example: four Characters cross two affected hexes in a Normal field. Enter 2 hexes and 4 entrants. Normal density checks up to two entrants per hex, producing four trigger checks.

pages.name: Triggers, Damage, and Blast
pages.content:
Triggers, Damage, and Blast

Each land exposure rolls the die set by the movement method. A result of 1 triggers a mine. The field's Condition then determines whether each triggered mine is a dud. Chat reports the number of checks, triggers, duds, and detonations.

Apply Direct Mine Damage

If at least one mine detonates, the GM can click Apply Direct Mine Damage. This applies the configured direct-hit profile once per detonation to the moving Actor. Direct hits against Characters and NPCs strike the legs. Vehicle hits use the vehicle damage and component systems.

Resolve the Blast

  1. On the canvas, select every nearby token that should be tested against the blast.
  2. Click Resolve Blast Against Selected Tokens on the minefield chat card.
  3. Confirm the Blast rating and any confined, airburst, or directional considerations.
  4. The system makes a separate, unpushable blast roll for each selected target and creates the normal damage and suppression controls in chat.

Target selection is deliberate: the system does not decide which tokens are inside a directional area or within the intended blast radius. The directly struck Actor can also be selected for the blast when appropriate.

Confined Areas

If the Scene has Confined-Space Hazards enabled, a detonation also offers Resolve Structural Collapse. Use it when the blast could damage the surrounding structure.

All minefield result buttons are GM controls. Each control marks its portion of the card as resolved so accidental repeated clicks do not apply the same result twice.

pages.name: Water Minefields
pages.content:
Water Minefields

Vehicle Preparation

The moving Actor must be a Vehicle with its Vehicle Domain set to Watercraft or Amphibious. Configure its vessel Size, crew, and driver. If it carries mine-detection equipment, enable that option on the watercraft configuration.

Region Settings

  • Set Environment to Water.
  • Contact: can be detected normally.
  • Bottom: requires suitable mine-detection equipment before the automatic detection attempt is available.
  • Mixed: represents a mixture of water-mine types.
  • Maximum Safe Vessel Size: vessels at or below this Size are ignored. Set it to 0 when every vessel Size should be at risk.

Crossing a Water Minefield

An undiscovered field first attempts detection when detection is possible. Once the field is Discovered, the assigned driver—or the first crew member if no driver is assigned—automatically rolls the configured Water-mine avoidance Skill. A success safely navigates the field.

If a water mine detonates, use the same chat-card controls as a land minefield. Direct Vehicle damage uses armor and component damage normally. A penetrating water-mine hit can force a hull breach. Select occupants or other nearby tokens before resolving any blast that should affect them.

Water movement ignores land Mine Type and land Density limits when determining whether a vessel is eligible. Vessel domain, Size, water-mine type, detection equipment, and discovery state are the important settings.

pages.name: GM Checklist and Troubleshooting
pages.content:
GM Checklist

  • The Scene has a Region covering the intended area.
  • The Region has an enabled Minefield Behavior.
  • The active GM is connected.
  • The moving token's Actor type matches the Mine Type or water settings.
  • The movement crosses the Region boundary or occurs within the Region.
  • The scout has the Skill configured under Action Skills.
  • Nearby tokens are selected before Resolve Blast is clicked.

If No Movement Dialog Appears

  • Confirm that the token actually entered or moved within the Region rather than being teleported without a movement event.
  • For land fields, check that Anti-Personnel, Anti-Vehicle, or Mixed matches the Actor type.
  • For water fields, check Vehicle Domain and Maximum Safe Vessel Size.
  • Confirm that the Minefield Behavior still listens for Token Enter and Token Move Within events.
  • If multiple GMs are connected, look for the dialog on the primary active GM's client.

If No Detection Roll Appears

  • A Discovered field skips detection.
  • No detection roll is made when No detection check is selected.
  • The scout must be a Character or NPC with the configured Detect Mines Skill.
  • A Bottom water mine requires suitable mine-detection equipment.

Resetting or Removing a Minefield

To make a known field unknown again, clear Discovered on the Behavior. To make the area harmless without deleting it, set Density to False Minefield for a land field or disable the Behavior. Delete the Behavior or Region only when the hazard is no longer needed.

Testing Safely

Before play, test with a spare token and low damage. Confirm detection, chat buttons, blast selection, and any vehicle interaction. Restore Discovered to its intended starting state after the test.
